headline_marked: [[Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman to visit Japan]], $2B loans & $6.36B investment expected
headline: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman to visit Japan, $2B loans & $6.36B investment expected
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's upcoming visit to Japan is set to secure around $2 billion in loans and financial support, alongside $6.36 billion in private investment. The trip aims to elevate bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership, focusing
details: Bangladesh and Japan are set to sign memorandums of understanding (MoUs) for approximately $2 billion in loans and financial support during Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s official visit to Tokyo. This package will cover budgetary support, infrastructure development, and cooperation in energy and maritime security.

The visit, scheduled from October 26 to 29, includes a summit with Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi slated for October 27. Japan is also expected to facilitate around $6.36 billion in private-sector investment in Bangladesh over the next five years.

A diplomatic source indicated that about $300 million of the proposed loan amount is earmarked for budgetary support. Japan will likely advocate for regional connectivity, particularly the Moheshkhali-Matarbari Integrated Infrastructure Development Initiative (MIDI), aligning with its Free and Open Indo-Pacific (FOIP) vision.

Under Japan’s Official Security Assistance (OSA) programme, Tokyo is expected to provide a 35-foot vessel to the Bangladesh Coast Guard. This follows the earlier handover of five patrol boats to the Bangladesh Navy, marking Bangladesh’s first OSA project.

The visit is also poised to upgrade the relationship between the two nations to a comprehensive strategic partnership (CSP). State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam highlighted the significance of the visit, anticipating MoUs in various sectors including technology, garments, education, and health.

Japan's Bay of Bengal Industrial Growth Belt (BIG-B) initiative, launched in 2014, will also be a key discussion point, aiming to promote industrial development and connectivity. This includes linking production centers with global markets through infrastructure like the Matarbari deep-sea port.

headline_marked: [[HSC and equivalent exam results]] to be published on October 29, says Inter-Education Board
headline: HSC and equivalent exam results to be published on October 29, says Inter-Education Board
summary: The Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee announced the decision following a meeting with the education minister and secretary. Further details regarding the results will be released on October 26.
details: Results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are scheduled for publication on October 29. This announcement was made by the chairman of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee.
Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chair of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka, confirmed the decision on Saturday. The date was finalized after a meeting at the education ministry.
The meeting included the education secretary and the education minister. Additional information regarding the results will be officially announced on October 26.
caption:
The wait is almost over for HSC and equivalent exam candidates! Results for this year's examinations will be published on October 29.

Results of this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations are scheduled for publication on October 29. This announcement was made by the chairman of the Inter-Education Board Coordination Committee.

Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chair of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Dhaka, confirmed the decision on Saturday. The date was finalized after a meeting at the education ministry.

The meeting included the education secretary and the education minister. Additional information regarding the results will be officially announced on October 26.
